name: Question 10
problem: Given the curve $r(t)=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨{t}^{2},\,-2{t}^{2},\,-2⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s={t}^{2},$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
worked_solution:
First, since $s={t}^{2},$ we have that $t=\sqrt{s}.$

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt{s}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨{(\sqrt{s})}^{2},\,-2{(\sqrt{s})}^{2},\,-2⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨s,\,-2s,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, since the curve is parameterized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-2s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-2)⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨1,\,-2,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Given the curve r(t)=55⟨t2,−2t2,−2⟩, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=t2, find the corresponding unit tangent T(s), parametrized by s.

a
T(s)=66⟨1,−1,−2⟩
b
T(s)=13⟨1,−2,2⟩
c
T(s)=13⟨2,−1,−2⟩
d
T(s)=−55⟨1,0,2⟩
e
T(s)=55⟨1,−2,0⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, since s=t2, we have that t=s.

Therefore, the vector function R(s) that parametrizes r(t) by its arc length is given by R(s)=r(s)=55⟨(s)2,−2(s)2,−2⟩=55⟨s,−2s,−2⟩.

Now, since the curve is parameterized by its arc length s, the unit tangent can be found as T(s)=ddsR(s).

So, we obtain T(s)=ddsR(s)=55⟨dds(s),dds(−2s),dds(−2)⟩=55⟨1,−2,0⟩.
